sections.html:
Find the Recorder in the Administrative Courthouse, 210 East Main Street, Suite 205, Lancaster. Hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays, and the phone is 740-652-7100. This office holds the permanent public record for the county: deeds, mortgages, leases, liens, plats, powers of attorney and military discharges.

The land records index goes back to 1800, and scanned documents can be searched online from January 1980 on. Staff can point you to the right desk, but they will not run a search, help draft a document or hand out recording forms. Someone else, usually a closing agent or attorney, has to write the deed.

  • Search deeds and mortgages from the online land records link on the Recorder page.
  • Sign up there for the free Property Fraud Alert and Notary Fraud Alert.
  • Phone ahead before a trip. Short closures, such as a one-hour midday closing on a single day, get posted on that page.

A Fairfield County deed goes to the County Auditor before it reaches the Recorder. The Auditor completes the transfer, and only then does the deed go on to be recorded. A sale usually needs two papers at the Auditor: the deed and a conveyance fee statement, which is Ohio form DTE 100 (or DTE 100EX when an exemption applies).

The Auditor's Map Room compares the legal description with county conveyance standards before accepting the deed. You can email a prepared deed to the Map Room for that approval, and the transfer cannot proceed without it. Once approved, drop the deed and statement at the transfer desk, 108 N. High Street in Lancaster, or mail them to the Auditor marked Attn: Conveyance.

The buyer or the buyer's representative files the statement of value, and the seller pays the conveyance fee. Value means the full consideration paid or to be paid, mortgage included. For a gift, use the estimated open market price. Entering a false value on purpose is prohibited by R.C. 319.202.

Two separate bills apply: the Auditor's transfer and conveyance charges, and the Recorder's recording fee, which depends on page count.

Fees on a Fairfield County deed
ChargeRatePaid to
Transfer fee$.50 per parcel, exempt and non-exempt transfers alikeCounty Auditor
Conveyance fee$4.00 per thousand of consideration when money changes handsCounty Auditor
Recording, first two pages$17 base fee plus $17 housing trust fund feeCounty Recorder
Recording, each added page$4 base fee plus $4 housing trust fund feeCounty Recorder
Document preservation surchargeUp to $5, if the county charges itCounty Recorder

These rates come from the Auditor's conveyance fact sheet and Ohio Revised Code 317.32. The Recorder's own fee schedule is linked from the Recorder page, so check the surcharge and any other line there before you write a check. A county can also levy a real property transfer tax of up to 30 cents per $100 under R.C. 322.02. The grantor pays it to the Auditor before the Recorder sees the deed.

sections.h2: Who can acknowledge a deed, and where it is filed
sections.html:
The grantor must sign an Ohio deed, and the signature must be acknowledged before an authorized officer (R.C. 5301.01). The statute lists these officers:

  • a judge or clerk of a court of record in Ohio
  • a county auditor or county engineer
  • a notary public
  • a mayor

File the deed in the county where the land lies. Under R.C. 5301.25, an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later good faith buyer who knew nothing about it. For a Fairfield County house, the deed belongs on file in Lancaster, whether the home sits in Pickerington, Canal Winchester, Reynoldsburg or an unincorporated township.

The Recorder logs each instrument in order of presentation, with the date and exact time. Under R.C. 317.13 the Recorder may decline an instrument that is materially false or fraudulent, and anyone whose paper is refused can ask the Court of Common Pleas to order it recorded.

Yes, Fairfield County deeds can be e-recorded through Simplifile, the route the Auditor's fact sheet names. A one-time filer may find that setup impractical and can use paper instead.

Ohio set a statutory target of June 30, 2026 for every county recorder, auditor and engineer to offer electronic recording of real property conveyances, and for recorders to post electronic indexes and images of instruments recorded since January 1, 1980. That matches the 1980 online start on the Fairfield page. A recorder may require a username and password to view those records but cannot charge for one.

Paper filing still works. Mail or drop off the deed with the Auditor, then send the Recorder its fee. Call 740-652-7100 to ask how to get the original returned to you.

sections.h2: Before you close on a Fairfield County sale
sections.html:
Fairfield County sits in the Columbus metropolitan area, with Lancaster as county seat and largest city. Population was 158,921 at the 2020 census. Franklin, Licking, Perry, Hocking and Pickaway counties surround it, and a mailing address in a neighboring county does not change where a Fairfield County parcel is recorded. Ask the city or township office where the house sits about any open permit before you list.

Because the Auditor, Recorder and Treasurer are separate offices, build a short checklist for closing: legal description approved, conveyance fee statement signed, taxes confirmed with the Treasurer, then recording.

  • Legal description cleared by the Auditor's Map Room
  • Deed signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer
  • Statement of value (DTE 100 or DTE 100EX) completed
  • Transfer and conveyance fees paid at the Auditor's transfer desk
  • Recording fee sent to the Recorder

A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, but every item above still applies. The title company usually handles the order of stops, and you supply the signature, a photo ID for the notary and your latest tax bill.

sections.h2: If you suspect fraud on your property
sections.html: Enroll in the Recorder's free alerts first. They flag new documents filed under your name or a notary's name. Then call the Recorder at 740-652-7100 to ask what was filed, and contact an attorney about next steps. For Veteran ID cards, the Recorder's office asks callers to use the same number.

faqs.q: Which office files a deed for a Fairfield County house?
faqs.a: The Fairfield County Recorder, 210 East Main Street, Suite 205, Lancaster, records it after the County Auditor has processed the transfer. The Auditor is a separate stop at 108 N. High Street.

faqs.q: What does the Auditor charge to transfer a deed in Fairfield County?
faqs.a: The Auditor's fact sheet lists a $.50 per parcel transfer fee and a conveyance fee of $4.00 per thousand of consideration when money changes hands. Ask the transfer desk to confirm the amount before you bring payment.

faqs.q: Does Fairfield County have its own deed form?
faqs.a: No. The Recorder does not provide recording forms and staff cannot help prepare a document. A title company or attorney usually drafts the deed, and the Auditor's Map Room reviews the legal description.

faqs.q: Can I look up old Fairfield County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes, partly. Indexes go back to 1800 and images are online from January 1980 forward through the Recorder's land records search. Older documents are at the office.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller does. Ohio law puts the conveyance fee on the grantor, while the buyer files the statement of value with the Auditor.
